results.reason: Issue 3 cites SA §13.2. It notes Norvane may assign 'to any third party' with no notice, while Calder Ridge cannot assign without consent. It explains the risk of drawings and supply passing to a competitor or weak assignee. It proposes mutual consent and a 'Supplier may not assign to a competitor' carve-out.

The memo cites SA §13.3: a change of control requires Norvane's consent and lets Norvane terminate. It explains the leverage this gives over a sale, merger or financing. It recommends deletion, or limiting the trigger to competitor acquirers with notice and a last-time-buy right. It does not mention a specific pending sale, but asks about corporate plans.

The memo cites OF §2.2: successive 3-year renewals unless notice is given 30 days before expiry, and late notice has no effect. It explains the lock-in risk and proposes one-year renewals, 90 days' notice and a reminder obligation.
Issue 1 notes that §9.3 exempts only Calder Ridge's indemnity from the cap, while Norvane's §10.2 indemnity remains 'subject to Section 9.1'. It proposes making the carve-out mutual.
The memo correctly states the cap as fees paid in the prior 12 months (§9.1), Delaware law (§12.1) and an Effective Date of March 1, 2026 with a 3-year Initial Term ending around February 2029.
The memo states the §1.3 hierarchy (SA, then OF, then Sched.). It notes the SA controls the renewal conflict with OF §2.2 and the invoice timing conflict.
A priority table ranks the issues Critical, High, Medium and Low. The uncapped indemnity is #1 (Critical) and change of control is #3 (High), both ahead of lesser issues.
Each issue has 'Where', 'Why it matters' and 'Fix' with proposed language. A separate 'Business Questions and Items Needing Client Input' section appears at the end.

The memo treats the Specifications Schedule as a source of significant issues. It ranks the OF/Schedule mismatch as a Critical issue, and also flags the Schedule's AQL sampling, missing head standards and 'Acknowledged' signature block.
